samples.text: For the moment the period is running on a workaround: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. The basis for that override is the confirmed cause, stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, so the override corrects the codes the run reads rather than masking a failure somewhere else. It holds for this period only, and no permanent correction to the mapping is in place at the time of writing. This position is provisional and will be revisited once the incident review settles the longer-term fix. People deciding whether to wait can act on the current output for this period, because the override was applied to the data the valuation actually uses. They should not assume the same protection carries into the next run. The stale mapping is still the source, and until it is corrected at source each new period starts with the same exposure. Teams with work due on the next valuation should plan for a check of their inputs

The established cause is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. The valuation run resolved agency codes through that mapping, and an entry that no longer matched the cloud code set was enough to stop the run. Our first working explanation was different: the failure was initially recorded as an overnight ERP outage, and that was the position for most of the morning. That hypothesis was ruled out on evidence, not on argument, because ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. Classification has since moved past the data fault to the control around it: control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
